All welcome St Seachnall’s Day - Friday 27th Nov The Church of St Seachnall refers to the Ancient Church founded by St Seachnall or Secondinus. Seachnall came to Ireland with his brother Auxilius in 439 AD. He established his Church. He Became Bishop of the See of Duns haughlin and became known as St Patrick’s bishop. Later St Patrick called him to Armagh as Auxiliary Bishop he died at the age of 75 and was buried in St Sea chnall’s Church. He wrote two Hymns one in Praise of St Patrick the other about t he Eucharist. A legend says the hymn was performed by Angels in the Cathedral in Dunshaughlin. The Historical Society have organised an Ecumenical Ceremony in St Seachnall’s Cof I Church for 11 am Friday There will be Prayers, Readings, poetry and music. The event is hosted by Reverend Clement, Cof I Pastor Our Pastoral Area is known as St Seachnall P. A. Youth Retreat Christmas Retreat organised by Youth 2000 in Newbridge College, Co. Points to Ponder In today’s Gospel, Jesus draws from this revelation about the future the fu ture the practical moral that a Christian needs to be on the watch, living each day as if it were his last. The important thing is not to speculate about when these events will happen and what form they will take, but to live in such a way that they Įnd us in the state of grace.
Living each day as if it were your last is a powerful concept that can help us to live more fully and with greater purpose.
It reminds us that our time on this earth is limited and that we should make the most of every moment.
It also enco urages us to focus on what is truly important in life, such as our relationships with others and our relationsh ip with God.
Keeping watch is another important aspect of this passage.
It reminds us to be vigilant and to stay alert t6o the signs of the times.
